# Xymon Status Icons: Complete Reference

Reference for the Xymon monitoring status-icon system (the colored GIF dots/flags shown
on Xymon status boards), for building a similar-looking monitoring app.

Source: Xymon source tree, `xymond/wwwfiles/gifs/` + `lib/color.c`.

---

## The 6 Status Colors (plus Unknown)

Every test and every host in Xymon is assigned one status color. The color is the
single most important piece of visual information on the board.

| Color | Means | Triggered when | Operator action |
|-------|-------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Green** | Status is OK | Test passed, all good | Nothing — this is the happy state |
| **Yellow** | Warning | A warning threshold was exceeded (e.g. disk > 80%) | Investigate; something is degrading but not yet broken |
| **Red** | Critical | A panic threshold was exceeded, or a service is down | Act now; a service is out or data is being lost |
| **Clear** | No data | The test ran but produced no meaningful output | Usually a config problem on the test/collector side |
| **Purple** | No report | The host/test is expected to report but hasn't sent data | A collector/agent died, or a scheduled job didn't run |
| **Blue** | Disabled | The test was intentionally turned off | Acknowledge it is deliberate; look for hosts left disabled after maintenance |
| **Unknown** | Indeterminate | Xymon cannot determine the status (e.g. no history at all) | Check the test's history/log; usually first-run or config issue |

Color priority (worst -> best): **red > yellow > purple > clear > blue > green**.
A host's overall icon is the **worst** (highest-priority) color among its tests.
Unknown is outside this ranking and treated as "can't tell yet" rather than worse or better.

---

## Reading the Board at a Glance

For an operator, the status column answers three questions in one icon:

1. **How bad is it?** — the color (green = fine, yellow/red = broken).
2. **Is it new or long-standing?** — `-recent` variant = changed within 24h.
3. **Has someone claimed it?** — the `-ack` variant = acknowledged by a user.

After 24 hours, an unchanged status "ages out" from `-recent` to the plain icon, so
an old alarm looks calmer than a fresh one even if the severity is the same.

---

## The Three Icon Variants

Each color has up to **three display variants**, distinguished by GIF filename:

| Variant | Filename | Shown when |
|---------|----------|------------|
| Stable | `{color}.gif` (e.g. `red.gif`) | Status has been unchanged for **more than 24 hours** |
| Recent | `{color}-recent.gif` (e.g. `red-recent.gif`) | Status **changed within the last 24 hours** |
| Acknowledged | `{color}-ack.gif` (e.g. `red-ack.gif`) | The status has been **acknowledged** by a user |

The **recent** variants are face icons that pulse/flash to draw the eye to new changes.
The stable variants are either a static shape or a slow glow.

### Exact naming logic

From `lib/color.c` (`dotgiffilename(color, acked, oldage)`):

```
base = colorname(color)            # green|yellow|red|clear|blue|purple|unknown
if acked:    add "-ack"
else if recent-gifs enabled AND NOT old:  add "-recent"
suffix = "." + IMAGEFILETYPE       # .gif by default, skins may use .png/.xpm
```

- The 24-hour "recent" window is `recentgif_limit = 86400` seconds.
- Recent icons are switched on via `--recentgifs` (default on in normal operation).
- Ack wins over recent: an acknowledged status shows the ack icon regardless of age.
- Not every file exists for every color — Xymon will happily render a broken image
  if the skin lacks the file, so the shipped set must cover every path the logic can
  produce. Files NOT shipped: **`clear-ack.gif`** and **`unknown-ack.gif`**
  (nothing meaningful to acknowledge on "no data" / "unknown").

### Configurable column icons

The info/trends/client columns can use custom icons via env vars in `xymonserver.cfg`;
they default to `green.gif`:

```
INFOCOLUMNGIF=green.gif
TRENDSCOLUMNGIF=green.gif
CLIENTCOLUMNGIF=green.gif
```

### Host icon

A host's overall icon is `dotgiffilename` of the host's **worst-status color** with the
same stable/recent/ack logic as individual tests.

## What Each Icon Looks Like, and What It Tells the Operator

### Stable status icons (16x16)

These are the "long-standing state" icons. Note they are NOT all the same shape —
green is a smooth ball, the alarm colors are faceted gems with diagonal bands, and
blue/clear are abstract shapes.

**`green.gif` — round green "globe" ball (static)**
- Solid green sphere with a bright highlight at upper-left and a darker shading
  bottom-right. Reader instantly reads "all is well".
- Key palette: highlight `#49f806`/`#38ff01`, mid-green `#49ab35`, dark `#3e5927`.
- Source: Big Sister "bigbro13" skin.

**`yellow.gif` — faceted amber gem / cut diamond (animated pulse, 14 frames, ~30ms each)**
- A yellow gem with diagonal facet bands and dark grooves; the palette cycles to make
  it visibly shimmer/glow so a warning never goes unnoticed.
- Key palette: body `#ff9900`, highlights `#f59300`/`#d2a800`, dark edges `#251e00`.
- Source: deadcat "animated-bb-icons" set (GPL).
- Operator meaning: degrading, worth watching — the shimmer keeps it on your radar.

**`red.gif` — faceted red gem / cut diamond (animated pulse, 10 frames, ~50ms each)**
- Same faceted-gem design as yellow but deep red, with band faces alternating
  `#ff0000` and `#800000`. The palette cycling gives a "beating" flash.
- Source: deadcat "animated-bb-icons" set (GPL).
- Operator meaning: critical, act now — designed to jump out of a busy board.

**`blue.gif` — concentric circles (bullseye) inside a rounded square (static)**
- Rows of nested blue rings (dark blue `#000080` field, bright ring edges `#0000ff`,
  pale highlight `#90b4fb`). Reads as "paused/switched off".
- Source: deadcat "animated-bb-icons" set (GPL).
- Operator meaning: deliberately disabled — confirm it was you, not leftover config.

**`purple.gif` — pulsing purple dot (animated, 37 frames, ~100ms each)**
- A purple pixel-sphere that slowly brightens then dims over ~3.7s — a calm, slow
  "heartbeat" rather than an alarm flash. Base color `#e900ff`.
- Source: deadcat "animated-bb-icons" set (GPL).
- Operator meaning: expected to report but silent (agent down, job didn't run).

**`clear.gif` — empty window / sheet with a 2x2 grid (static)**
- A light rounded rectangle (`#cccccc` border, `#808080` field) with thin cross-lines
  dividing it into four panes — "nothing here".
- Source: deadcat "animated-bb-icons" set (GPL).
- Operator meaning: test produced no meaningful data; check the collector config.

**`unknown.gif` — gold question mark (static)**
- A yellow/gold `?` (`#fdcb03`) with pale highlights and grey shading — literally
  "we don't know yet". `unknown-recent.gif` is byte-identical.
- Source: `question.png` from brindilles.net (public domain theme smilie).

## Common shapes by status

| Status | Stable | Recent | Ack | Animation style |
|--------|--------|--------|-----|-----------------|
| Green | glossy ball | happy face | check | recent static |
| Yellow | faceted gem | happy face | check | slow shimmer (stable), pulse (recent) |
| Red | faceted gem | angry face | check | fast flash (stable), pulse (recent) |
| Blue | concentric rings | calm face | check | static (stable), pulse (recent) |
| Purple | pulsing dot | quiet face | check | slow heartbeat (stable), pulse (recent) |
| Clear | empty window grid | blank face | — | static / static |
| Unknown | question mark | question mark | — | static / static |

---

## Visual Appearance of the Icons

The shipped artwork is derived from public-domain/GPL collections
(see `gifs/README`), so the classic Xymon look is:

- **Stable icons** — the classic Big Brother style: **green** is a round glossy globe;
  **red / yellow / blue / purple / clear** are from the deadcat "animated-bb-icons"
  set — faceted gems (red/yellow), rings (blue), a pulsing dot (purple), and an
  empty window (clear).
- **Recent icons** — from the deadcat "smile" set (smiley faces) that **pulse/flash**
  by cycling the GIF color table rather than re-drawing pixels.
- **Ack icons** — solid 12x12 checkmarks in the status color, smaller than the 16x16
  status icons.
- **Unknown** — a **question mark**.
- **Zoom** — a magnifying-glass icon (taken from Cacti).

### Skinning / replacement

- Icons can be replaced wholesale by dropping new files (any size) into the gifs
  directory — no code changes needed. `BBSKIN`/`XYMONSKIN` lets you switch.
- The **extension is configurable** via `IMAGEFILETYPE` (default `gif`), so a skin
  can use PNG/XPM instead.
- Add-on icon packs exist (e.g. "sa_icons", LED themes) that replace faces with
  clean colored shapes for corporate/color-blind-friendly use.

---

## Design Takeaways for a Similar App

1. **Color is the primary signal** — icons are *rendered* in one of 6–7 colors and
   the status is instantly readable at a glance.
2. **Two recency states** distinguish "just broke" from "still broken":
   animate/flash when the status changed recently, go static after ~24h.
3. **Acknowledgment is a third visual state** that tells everyone "yes, we know".
4. **Worst-status aggregation**: a host takes the most severe color of any test.
5. **Alarm colors animate even when stable** — a red/yellow alarm never looks
   "settled" on a status board; only green/clear/unknown are calm when old.
6. **16x16 default icons** are the practical minimum for a dense status grid.
7. **Everything is skinnable** — statuses are just colored images; swap the images
   to restyle without touching logic.

---

## Appendix: Xymon Repo Notes (Style Context)

- Repo: `https://github.com/xymon-monitoring/xymon` (GPL-2.0, primarily C).
- The project uses **no emojis anywhere** in authored content (titles, commits,
  docs, labels) — deliberately formal and text-only. Do not add emojis to anything
  that lands in the tree.
- PR titles follow `component: sentence in lowercase` (e.g. `xymond: fix ...`).
- Icons were collected from GPL/public-domain archives; only freely-distributable
  artwork is used.
- Animation is implemented by **GIF palette cycling** (stable pixel indices, per-frame
  color-table remap) — the same trick is the cheapest way to add a "pulse" to your
  own icon set.
